question: What does the South Carolina CDL manual advise you use for safety purposes during the Vehicle Inspection test?
choice_a: Wheel chocks
choice_b: A jack stand under each axle
choice_c: Traffic cones around the vehicle
choice_d: A tow strap attached to the frame
explanation: The manual states, "[For safety purposes, you should use wheel chocks during the Vehicle Inspection test.]"
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, introductory instructions

question: When safely entering or exiting the vehicle during the inspection, how many points of contact must you maintain at all times?
choice_a: Two
choice_b: Three
choice_c: Four
choice_d: One
explanation: The manual requires drivers to "safely exit/enter by facing the vehicle and maintaining three (3) points of contact at all times."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, introductory instructions

question: During the CDL Vehicle Inspection test, how many vehicle axles will you actually be required to inspect, even though you should be prepared to perform the same inspection on all axles?
choice_a: All axles
choice_b: Two axles
choice_c: One axle
choice_d: Half of the axles
explanation: The manual states that "during the test, you will only be required to inspect one vehicle axle; however, you should be prepared to perform the same inspection described in section (11.5.2) on all of the vehicle axles."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, introductory instructions

question: What must you do for each safety critical item during the inspection in order to receive credit for it?
choice_a: Simply look at it and move on
choice_b: Ask the examiner to identify it for you
choice_c: Write its condition on the checklist
choice_d: Name, point to and/or touch, and fully explain to the examiner what you are inspecting the item for
explanation: The manual states, "You MUST name, point to and/or touch, and fully explain to the examiner WHAT you are inspecting each safety critical item for. If you do not, you will not get credit for the item(s)."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection, introductory instructions

question: If a vehicle is not equipped with electrical fuses, what must you do during the emergency equipment inspection?
choice_a: Mention this to the examiner and identify that the vehicle operates on circuit breakers
choice_b: Fail the vehicle inspection automatically
choice_c: Skip that inspection item entirely
choice_d: Assume spare fuses are stored elsewhere
explanation: The manual notes, "If the vehicle is not equipped with electrical fuses, you must mention this to the examiner and identify that the vehicle operates on circuit breakers."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.1, In-Vehicle/Engine Start, Emergency Equipment

question: The required emergency warning devices are three red reflective triangles, or what alternative combination?
choice_a: Two flashlights and one road flare
choice_b: Six fusee flares, or three liquid burning flares
choice_c: One warning sign and two cones
choice_d: Four fusee flares and two triangles
explanation: The manual lists the inspection item as "three (3) red reflective triangles, six (6) fusee flares, or three (3) liquid burning flares."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.1, In-Vehicle/Engine Start, Emergency Equipment

question: According to the manual, what is the only thing permitted on the windshield that is not treated as damage or an obstruction?
choice_a: A parking permit sticker
choice_b: A dealer advertisement sticker
choice_c: An inspection sticker
choice_d: A tinted strip along the top
explanation: The manual states the windshield must be "clean with no obstructions except for an inspection sticker," with no cracks or flaws to the glass.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.1, In-Vehicle/Engine Start, Windshield and Traffic Monitoring Devices

question: Besides inspecting that wiper arms and blades are secure and not damaged, what must you demonstrate about the wipers?
choice_a: That the wiper motor draws less than a specified amperage
choice_b: That the wiper blades can be removed without tools
choice_c: That the wipers are the same brand as the vehicle manufacturer
choice_d: That the wipers operate smoothly by turning them on and off
explanation: The manual requires you to "demonstrate wipers operate smoothly by turning them on and off."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.1, In-Vehicle/Engine Start, Wipers/Washers

question: How must you inspect the heater and defroster during the CDL Vehicle Inspection test?
choice_a: Identify, describe, and demonstrate that they work correctly by operating the controls
choice_b: Only check that the fuse for the heater is present
choice_c: Feel for warm air coming from the vents without using the controls
choice_d: Read the specifications from the owner's manual to the examiner
explanation: The manual requires you to "identify, describe, and demonstrate the heater(s) and defroster(s) work correctly by operating the controls."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.1, In-Vehicle/Engine Start, Heater/Defroster

question: What must you inspect regarding the vehicle's horn(s)?
choice_a: That there are at least two separate horns installed
choice_b: That the air horn and/or electric horn work
choice_c: That the horn button is illuminated
choice_d: That the horn wiring is color-coded per manufacturer standards
explanation: The manual's inspection requirement for horns simply states, "Inspect that air horn and/or electric horn work."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.1, In-Vehicle/Engine Start, Horn(s)

question: During the parking brake check, with the parking brake engaged and your foot removed from the service brake, how do you confirm the parking brake holds the vehicle?
choice_a: By revving the engine to full throttle
choice_b: By shifting into reverse and accelerating
choice_c: By gently pulling forward with the parking brake on
choice_d: By releasing the parking brake immediately after engaging it
explanation: The manual states you must "remove foot from service brake and inspect that the parking brake will hold the vehicle by gently pulling forward with the parking brake on."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.1, In-Vehicle/Engine Start, Parking and Trailer Brake Check

question: Besides confirming that the trailer parking brake holds the vehicle, what else does the trailer brake check help verify on combination vehicles?
choice_a: The tire pressure of the trailer axle
choice_b: The alignment of the headlights
choice_c: The fuel level in the trailer tank
choice_d: The coupling connection with the trailer
explanation: The manual states the trailer brake check "also assists in checking the coupling connection with the trailer."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.1, In-Vehicle/Engine Start, Parking and Trailer Brake Check

question: During the service brake check, at what speed do you pull forward before applying the service brake and coming to a complete stop?
choice_a: 5 mph
choice_b: 10 mph
choice_c: 15 mph
choice_d: 20 mph
explanation: The manual instructs, "Pull forward at 5 mph, apply the service (foot) brake and come to a complete stop."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.1, In-Vehicle/Engine Start, Service Brake Check

question: On a combination vehicle, in addition to checking the dashboard ABS indicator, what other ABS-related check should you perform?
choice_a: Confirm the rear driver's side trailer ABS light turns on then off
choice_b: Confirm the front bumper ABS light stays illuminated continuously
choice_c: Confirm the trailer brake light flashes rapidly
choice_d: Confirm the steering wheel ABS light never illuminates
explanation: The manual specifies that "for combination vehicles only, the rear driver's side trailer ABS light should turn on then off," if equipped.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.1, In-Vehicle/Engine Start, Lighting Indicators

question: What happens if you fail to explain and demonstrate (perform) all four parts of the air brake check correctly?
choice_a: You receive a warning but may continue
choice_b: You must repeat only the failed part
choice_c: It results in an automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test
choice_d: Nothing, since the air brake check is optional
explanation: The manual states, "Failure to explain and demonstrate (perform) all four (4) parts of the air brake check correctly will result in an automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.2, Air Brake Check

question: When building air pressure to governor cutout during the Air Gauge and Governor Cutout Check, at approximately what psi range does cutout occur (or as specified by the manufacturer)?
explanation: The manual states governor cutout "will occur at approximately 120 - 140 psi OR level specified by the manufacturer."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.2, Air Brake Check, Step 1: Air Gauge and Governor Cutout Check

topic: Air Leakage Rate Test - Single Vehicle
question: During the Air Leakage Rate Test, after holding the foot brake for one minute, how much can the air pressure drop for a single vehicle or trailer without air brakes?
choice_a: No more than three pounds
choice_b: No more than five pounds
choice_c: No more than eight pounds
choice_d: No more than one pound
explanation: The manual states air pressure should drop "no more than three (3) pounds in one (1) minute (single vehicle or trailer without airbrakes)" after initial stabilization.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.2, Air Brake Check, Step 2: Air Leakage Rate Test

topic: Air Leakage Rate Test - Combination Vehicle
question: For a combination vehicle, how much air pressure drop is allowed in one minute during the Air Leakage Rate Test?
choice_a: Two pounds
choice_b: Four pounds
choice_c: Six pounds
choice_d: Ten pounds
explanation: The manual allows the air pressure to drop "no more than ... four (4) pounds in one (1) minute (combination vehicle) after initial stabilization."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.2, Air Brake Check, Step 2: Air Leakage Rate Test

question: The low air warning devices (buzzer, light, and flag) should activate before air pressure drops below what level?
choice_a: 35 psi
choice_b: 45 psi
choice_c: 65 psi
choice_d: 55 psi
explanation: The manual states, "The low air warning devices (buzzer, light, and flag) should activate before air pressure drops below 55 psi."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.2, Air Brake Check, Step 3: Air Warning Device(s) Test

question: During the Emergency Brake(s) Test, at what psi range should the parking brake (or emergency brake) valve close (pop out)?
choice_a: 10 psi to 30 psi
choice_b: 30 psi to 60 psi
choice_c: 50 psi to 70 psi
choice_d: 20 psi to 45 psi
explanation: The manual states the valve "should close (pop out) between 20 psi and 45 psi (no less than 20 psi and no more than 45 psi) OR level specified by the manufacturer."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.2, Air Brake Check, Step 4: Emergency Brake(s) Test

topic: Emergency Brake Test - Trailer Valve Timing
question: On air-operated trailers, when should the tractor protection valve and trailer parking brake (or emergency brake) valve close relative to the truck/tractor/bus valve?
choice_a: At the same time or prior to the valve for the truck/tractor/bus
choice_b: Only several seconds after the truck valve closes
choice_c: Only after the driver manually engages the trailer brake
choice_d: Never, since trailer and tractor valves operate independently
explanation: The manual states "the tractor protection valve and trailer parking brake (or emergency brake) valve should close (pop out) at the same time or prior to the valve for the truck/tractor/bus."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.2, Air Brake Check, Step 4: Emergency Brake(s) Test

question: What happens if you fail to explain and demonstrate the hydraulic brake check correctly?
choice_a: You receive a minor point deduction
choice_b: It results in an automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test
choice_c: You are given a second attempt later in the test
choice_d: The examiner performs the check for you
explanation: The manual states, "Failure to explain and demonstrate the hydraulic brake check correctly will result in an automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.2, Hydraulic Brake Check

question: With the transmission placed in "park," the hydraulic brake pedal check involves pumping the brake pedal how many times and then holding it down for how long (or as specified by the manufacturer)?
choice_a: Pump it once, hold for ten seconds
choice_b: Pump it five times, hold for two seconds
choice_c: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down for five seconds
choice_d: Pump it ten times, hold for one second
explanation: The manual instructs to "pump the brake pedal three (3) times, and then hold it down for five (5) seconds], or as specified by the manufacturer."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.1.2, Hydraulic Brake Check

question: During the Passenger Entry and Lift inspection, what must you check about the entry steps?
choice_a: That they fold up automatically when the door closes
choice_b: That they are painted a bright warning color
choice_c: That they are made of non-slip rubber only
choice_d: That the entry steps are clear, and the tread is not loose or worn
explanation: The manual requires you to "inspect that the entry steps are clear, and the tread is not loose, or worn."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.2, Passenger and School Bus Only, Passenger Entry and Lift

question: If the bus is equipped with a passenger lift, what condition must the lift be in as part of the checklist item?
choice_a: It must be fully retracted and latched securely
choice_b: It must be left partially extended for quick access
choice_c: It must be removed and stored separately
choice_d: It must be covered by a protective tarp
explanation: The manual states, "If equipped, lift must be fully retracted and latched securely."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.2, Passenger and School Bus Only, Passenger Entry and Lift

question: During the Emergency Exits inspection, how many emergency exits must you actually demonstrate operate smoothly, close securely, and are not damaged?
choice_a: None, only a description is required
choice_b: All emergency exits on the vehicle
choice_c: At least one
choice_d: Exactly three
explanation: The manual requires you to "demonstrate that at least one (1) emergency exit operates smoothly, closes securely, and is not damaged," while pointing out and describing how all other emergency exits operate.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.2, Passenger and School Bus Only, Emergency Exits

question: What must you inspect regarding passenger seat frames?
choice_a: That the seats recline to a specific angle
choice_b: That the seats are removable for cargo storage
choice_c: That there are no broken seat frames and that they are firmly attached to the floor
choice_d: That the seat cushions are a uniform color
explanation: The manual requires you to "inspect that there are no broken seat frames and inspect that seat frames are firmly attached to the floor."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.2, Passenger and School Bus Only, Passenger Seating

question: Which lights must be inspected, with their operation demonstrated, on both the front and back of a school bus under the Student Lights checklist item?
choice_a: Only the headlights and taillights
choice_b: Only the four-way emergency flashers
choice_c: Only the license plate light
choice_d: Strobe light (if equipped), alternately flashing amber lights, and alternately flashing red lights
explanation: The manual lists that "strobe light (if equipped)," "alternately flashing amber lights," and "alternately flashing red lights" must all be inspected and demonstrated on both the front and back of the vehicle, along with their dashboard indicators.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.3, School Bus Only, Student Lights (Front and Back)

question: What is the purpose of the stop arm on a school bus, according to the manual?
choice_a: It warns other drivers a school bus is stopping or is stopped
choice_b: It measures the vehicle's current speed
choice_c: It indicates that the fuel level is low
choice_d: It signals a mechanical transmission failure
explanation: The manual states, "Stop Arm - Warns other drivers a school bus is stopping or is stopped."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.3, School Bus Only, Stop Arm(s) and Safety Arm

question: The safety arm on a school bus forces students to cross how far away from the front of the bus, in the driver's view?
choice_a: 5 feet
choice_b: 10 feet
choice_c: 15 feet
choice_d: 20 feet
explanation: The manual describes the safety arm as forcing "school students to cross well (e.g., 10 feet) away from the front of the school bus in the drivers view."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.3, School Bus Only, Stop Arm(s) and Safety Arm

topic: First Aid and Body Fluid Kits
question: When inspecting the emergency first aid kit and body fluid cleanup kit on a school bus, what condition may indicate that items are missing?
choice_a: The kit's outer case is a faded color
choice_b: The kit is stored in the rear of the bus
choice_c: The seal has been broken
choice_d: The kit was manufactured more than a year ago
explanation: The manual states to "inspect that emergency first aid kit is present and the seal has not been broken which may indicate missing items," and the same for the body fluid cleanup kit.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.3, School Bus Only, First Aid Emergency and Body Fluid Kits

question: During the Lights Operations Check on a combination vehicle, which portion of the trailer must you inspect?
choice_a: Only the front of the trailer
choice_b: Only the sides of the trailer
choice_c: You need only inspect the rear of the trailer
choice_d: The entire trailer undercarriage
explanation: The manual notes, "on a combination vehicle, you need only inspect the rear of the trailer" during the Lights Operations Check.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.4, Lights Operations Check (All Vehicles)

question: How must the operation of all external lights be inspected?
choice_a: From inside the vehicle only, using the dashboard indicators
choice_b: From outside the vehicle
choice_c: Using only a rearview mirror
choice_d: External lights do not need to be physically inspected
explanation: The manual states, "The operation of all external lights must be inspected from outside the vehicle, including lights activated by an automated light check system."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.4, Lights Operations Check (All Vehicles)

question: What must brake lights do when the brakes are applied and released, per the Lights Operations Check?
choice_a: Come "on" when brakes are applied and turn "off" when brakes are released
choice_b: Stay illuminated continuously regardless of brake use
choice_c: Flash on and off regardless of brake application
choice_d: Only illuminate when the parking brake is set
explanation: The manual requires you to "inspect that brake lights come 'on' when brakes are applied and turn 'off' when brakes are released."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.4, Lights Operations Check (All Vehicles)

question: What must you inspect regarding the light lenses or covers on the front of the vehicle/tractor?
choice_a: That they are the proper color, clean, not broken and not missing
choice_b: That they are tinted to reduce glare
choice_c: That they are made of tempered glass
choice_d: That they match the color of the vehicle body
explanation: The manual requires you to "inspect that light lenses or covers are the proper color, clean, not broken and not missing."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.1, Front of Vehicle / Engine Area (Engine Off), Lenses

question: Among the critical fluid levels inspected with the engine off, which one is inspected only on vehicles equipped with hydraulic brakes?
choice_a: Engine oil
choice_b: Brake fluid
choice_c: Coolant
choice_d: Power steering fluid
explanation: The manual lists "brake fluid for vehicle braking (hydraulic brakes only)" among the fluids to inspect, distinguishing it from engine oil, coolant, and power steering fluid, which apply more broadly.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.1, Front of Vehicle / Engine Area (Engine Off), Critical Fluid Levels

question: When identifying fluid levels at the dipstick(s) or sight glass(es), where should the fluid level be?
choice_a: Above the full mark
choice_b: At the very bottom of the reservoir
choice_c: Between the add and the full marks
choice_d: Exactly level with the add mark only
explanation: The manual states you should "identify that you would inspect that the level is between the add and the full marks for each item."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.1, Front of Vehicle / Engine Area (Engine Off), Critical Fluid Levels

question: What caution does the manual give regarding the radiator cap during the fluid level inspection?
choice_a: Always remove it to check coolant color
choice_b: If the engine is hot, do not remove the radiator cap
choice_c: Remove it only after the engine has run for one hour
choice_d: Tighten it before checking any other fluids
explanation: The manual gives the explicit caution: "If the engine is hot, do not remove the radiator cap."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.1, Front of Vehicle / Engine Area (Engine Off), Critical Fluid Levels

question: What must you inspect regarding the power steering box?
choice_a: That it is painted to match the frame
choice_b: That it is chrome-plated for corrosion resistance
choice_c: That it is securely mounted and not leaking
choice_d: That it can be removed without tools
explanation: The manual requires you to "inspect that the power steering box is securely mounted and not leaking."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.1, Front of Vehicle / Engine Area (Engine Off), Steering System

question: What is the minimum tread depth required on steering axle tires, as tested with a tread depth gauge on major tread grooves containing wear bars?
choice_a: 2/32 inch
choice_b: 6/32 inch
choice_c: 8/32 inch
choice_d: 4/32 inch
explanation: The manual specifies minimum tread depth of "4/32 on steering axle tires, 2/32 on all other tires."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.2, Axle Components/Steering Axle, Tires

question: What is the minimum tread depth required on tires other than steering axle tires?
choice_a: 4/32 inch
choice_b: 2/32 inch
choice_c: 1/32 inch
choice_d: 6/32 inch
explanation: The manual specifies minimum tread depth of "4/32 on steering axle tires, 2/32 on all other tires."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.2, Axle Components/Steering Axle, Tires

question: How must you check tire inflation in order to receive credit during the inspection?
choice_a: By kicking the tire
choice_b: Using a tire gauge
choice_c: By striking it with a mallet
choice_d: By visual estimate of sidewall bulge
explanation: The manual states, "You will not get credit if you simply kick the tires or use a mallet to inspect for proper inflation. You must mention the use of a tire gauge."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.2, Axle Components/Steering Axle, Tires

question: When inspecting tire condition on dual tires, what specific mismatch should you look for?
choice_a: Mismatched diameters
choice_b: Mismatched brand names
choice_c: Mismatched valve cap colors
choice_d: Mismatched manufacture dates only
explanation: The manual requires you to "look for bumps and bulges in the sidewall and mismatched diameters in dual tires."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.2, Axle Components/Steering Axle, Tires

question: If tires are equipped with an automatic tire inflation system (ATIS) or tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) with hoses connected to the valve stems, what must you do during inspection?
choice_a: Ignore the tires since they are self-monitoring
choice_b: Mention that tire pressure is monitored and adjusted by an automatic system and inspect that it is working properly
choice_c: Automatically fail the vehicle for having non-standard equipment
choice_d: Disconnect the system before checking pressure manually
explanation: The manual states, "you need only mention that tire pressure is monitored and adjusted by an automatic system and inspect that it is working properly."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.2, Axle Components/Steering Axle, Tires

question: What repair is explicitly not permitted on a damaged or cracked rim, according to the manual?
choice_a: Welding repairs
choice_b: Bolt tightening
choice_c: Cleaning with a wire brush
choice_d: Repainting
explanation: The manual states, "Inspect for damaged, cracked, or bent rims. Rims cannot have welding repairs."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.2, Axle Components/Steering Axle, Rims

question: What signs, besides lug nuts simply being loose, may indicate looseness during the lug nut inspection?
choice_a: A dull matte surface finish
choice_b: Rust trails or shiny threads
choice_c: Fresh paint on the nuts
choice_d: A missing hubcap only
explanation: The manual requires you to "inspect that lug nuts are not loose and there are no signs of rust trails or shiny threads that may show looseness."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.2, Axle Components/Steering Axle, Lug Nuts

question: What must you inspect regarding U-bolts and mounting bolts on the suspension?
choice_a: That they are painted a distinct color
choice_b: That they match in length only
choice_c: That they are not broken, missing, or loose
choice_d: That they are chrome-plated
explanation: The manual requires you to "inspect that U-bolts and mounting bolts are not broken, missing, or loose."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.2, Axle Components/Steering Axle, Springs/Mounts, U-Bolts and Air Bags and Shocks

question: What must you inspect regarding the battery's electrical connections, wherever the battery is located?
choice_a: That connections are tight and should not show signs of excessive corrosion
choice_b: That connections are painted for identification
choice_c: That connections are labeled with an installation date
choice_d: That connections can be removed without tools
explanation: The manual requires you to "inspect that all connections are tight and should not show signs of excessive corrosion, if visible."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.3, Side of Vehicle, Battery

question: What must you verify about the fuel tank, including a Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) tank if equipped?
choice_a: That it is painted red for visibility
choice_b: That it is securely mounted, the cap is tight, and there are no leaks from the tank or line
choice_c: That it is completely full at all times
choice_d: That it is insulated against temperature changes
explanation: The manual requires you to "inspect that the fuel tank, including a Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) tank, if equipped, is securely mounted, the cap is tight, and there are no leaks from the tank or line."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.3, Side of Vehicle, Fuel Tank/DEF Tank

question: Besides inspecting the frame members for cracks, broken welds, or holes, what other area must you also inspect for cracks, breaks, or holes?
choice_a: The dashboard housing
choice_b: The cargo area or floor
choice_c: The windshield frame
choice_d: The seat cushions
explanation: The manual requires you to "inspect for cracks, breaks, or holes in the cargo area or floor, including the trailer, if applicable."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.3, Side of Vehicle, Frame(s)

question: What type of contamination is inspected on the brake lining/pads and the brake drum or disc?
choice_a: Water residue only
choice_b: Road salt only
choice_c: Grease, oil, etc.
choice_d: Dust buildup only
explanation: The manual instructs you to "inspect for contaminants such as grease, oil, etc., on the brake lining or pads and the brake drum or disc that can affect braking capabilities."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.2, Axle Components/Steering Axle, Brake Contaminates

question: What must you inspect regarding light lenses/covers and reflectors on the sides of the vehicle and trailer?
choice_a: That they are the proper color, clean, not broken, or missing
choice_b: That they are the same brand across the vehicle
choice_c: That they are recessed into the body panel
choice_d: That they are removable for cleaning
explanation: The manual requires that side lenses/covers and reflectors be inspected to confirm they "are the proper color, clean, not broken, or missing."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.3, Side of Vehicle, Lenses and Reflectors

question: What must you inspect regarding light lenses/covers and reflectors on the rear of the vehicle or trailer?
choice_a: That they are angled at exactly 45 degrees
choice_b: That they are made of shatterproof plastic only
choice_c: That they are mounted higher than the taillights
choice_d: That they are the proper color, clean, not broken and not missing
explanation: The manual requires the rear "light lenses or covers" and "reflectors" to be "the proper color, clean, not broken and not missing."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.5.4, Rear of Vehicle or Trailer, Lenses and Reflectors

question: What must you inspect regarding the air and electric connectors on the power unit and trailer of a combination vehicle?
choice_a: That they are seated and sealed, free of damage and locked into place
choice_b: That they are color-coded to the manufacturer's paint scheme
choice_c: That they are removable without tools for quick disconnect
choice_d: That they are covered with a protective tarp during travel
explanation: The manual requires you to "inspect that air and electric connectors on the power unit and trailer are seated and sealed, free of damage and locked into place."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.6.1, Combination Vehicles Only, Air and Electric Lines / Connectors

question: When inspecting air hoses and electrical lines on a combination vehicle, what condition must NOT be present, and what must not be visible through worn areas?
choice_a: The hoses must not be longer than the trailer's wheelbase
choice_b: The hoses must not be a different color than the tractor's hoses
choice_c: The hoses must not be routed along the frame rail
choice_d: The hoses must not be cut, cracked, chafed, spliced, taped, or worn, with the steel braid/electrical conductor not showing through
explanation: The manual requires that hoses and lines "are not cut, cracked, chafed, spliced, taped, or worn (steel braid/electrical conductor must not show through)."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.6.1, Combination Vehicles Only, Air and Electric Lines / Connectors

question: To receive credit for the air and electric line connectors inspection on a combination vehicle, what must you inspect?
choice_a: Only the connections on the power unit
choice_b: Only the connections on the trailer
choice_c: The connections on both the power unit and trailer
choice_d: Only the connections visible from the driver's seat
explanation: The manual states, "You must inspect the connections on both the power unit and trailer to receive credit."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.6.1, Combination Vehicles Only, Air and Electric Lines / Connectors

topic: Fifth Wheel Skid Plate and Gap
question: For fifth wheel combinations, what must you confirm about the space between the apron and the fifth wheel skid plate?
choice_a: That there is at least a one-inch gap for lubrication
choice_b: That the gap is adjustable using a hand crank
choice_c: That the gap widens as the trailer turns
choice_d: That the trailer is lying flat on the skid plate with no space (no gap) between the apron and fifth wheel
explanation: The manual requires you to "inspect that the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate and there is no space between the apron and fifth wheel (no gap)."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.6.1, Combination Vehicles Only, Kingpin, Apron & Gap (Fifth Wheel Combinations)

question: What must you inspect regarding the kingpin on a fifth wheel combination?
choice_a: That it is painted a bright color for visibility
choice_b: That it is in place and not bent, damaged or worn
choice_c: That it is removable for cleaning
choice_d: That it is longer than the trailer's drawbar
explanation: The manual requires you to "inspect that the kingpin is in place and not bent, damaged or worn."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.6.1, Combination Vehicles Only, Kingpin, Apron & Gap (Fifth Wheel Combinations)

question: For pintle hook combinations, what must you inspect regarding the mounting of the pintle hook?
choice_a: That it is coated in a rust-preventative spray
choice_b: That it is bolted directly to the bumper
choice_c: That it is securely mounted to the vehicle frame
choice_d: That it swivels freely in all directions
explanation: The manual requires you to "inspect that the pintle hook is securely mounted to the vehicle frame."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.6.1, Combination Vehicles Only, Pintle Hook (Pintle Hook Combinations)

question: What must you inspect about the trailer drawbar ring or eye on pintle hook combinations?
choice_a: That it is chrome-plated
choice_b: That it is exactly the same diameter as the trailer tongue
choice_c: That it is painted to match the pintle hook
choice_d: That it is not bent or twisted
explanation: The manual requires you to "inspect that the drawbar ring or eye is not bent or twisted."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.6.1, Combination Vehicles Only, Trailer Drawbar Ring & Tongue (Pintle Hook Combinations)

question: For all other types of combinations using a tow or receiver hitch, what must you inspect besides secure mounting to the vehicle frame?
choice_a: The paint finish on the hitch ball
choice_b: The distance between the hitch and the rear bumper
choice_c: The sway bar/control, if equipped
choice_d: The manufacturer's warranty sticker
explanation: The manual states, "Inspect that the tow hitch or other mechanism is securely mounted to the vehicle frame. Inspect sway bar/control, if equipped."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.6.1, Combination Vehicles Only, Tow Hitch (All Other Types of Combinations)

topic: Locking and Safety Devices - Fifth Wheel
question: For fifth wheel coupling systems, what must you inspect by looking into the fifth wheel gap?
choice_a: That the gap is filled with grease at all times
choice_b: That a warning light is mounted inside the gap
choice_c: That the gap is wide enough to insert a hand
choice_d: That locking jaws or lever are fully secured around the kingpin, with no play between kingpin and locking jaws/lever
explanation: The manual states, "Look into fifth wheel gap and inspect that locking jaws or lever are fully secured around the kingpin and inspect for play between kingpin and locking jaws/lever."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.6.1, Combination Vehicles Only, Locking and Safety Devices (Fifth Wheel Coupling Systems)

question: What must you inspect regarding the landing gear on a trailer?
choice_a: That it is lowered halfway during travel for stability
choice_b: That it is painted the same color as the trailer frame
choice_c: That it is fully raised, has no missing parts, the crank handle is secure, and the support frame and landing pads are not damaged
choice_d: That it is removed entirely on tractor semi-trailers
explanation: The manual requires you to "inspect that the landing gear is fully raised, has no missing parts, the crank handle is secure, and the support frame and landing pads are not damaged."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.6.2, Trailers Only, Landing Gear & Clearance

question: According to the manual, reflective tape is only required for which type of vehicle, though some jurisdictions may also require it for school buses?
choice_a: Straight trucks
choice_b: Passenger buses
choice_c: Motorcoaches
choice_d: Trailers
explanation: The manual states, "Reflective tape is only required for trailers. Some jurisdictional laws may require reflective tape for school buses."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11.6.2, Trailers Only, Reflective Tape

question: On the CDL Vehicle Inspection checklists, an asterisk (*) is used to mark which items as causing automatic failure if not performed correctly?
choice_a: The air or hydraulic brake check
choice_b: The windshield wiper check
choice_c: The reflective tape inspection
choice_d: The horn inspection
explanation: On the Class A, Class B/C, and Passenger/School Bus checklists, the "*air or *hydraulic brake check" item is marked with a note stating, "* Automatic failure if not performed correctly."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection Checklists
